openTPU is an AI chip that says it was developed by AI, to run AI.
A developer open-sourced it on October 6th: hardware, compiler and simulator, in one repo.
It runs real language models on an old Kintex-7 FPGA card.
No cache. No hidden scheduling. Every data move is one visible instruction.
So a profiler can show exactly where every clock cycle goes.
The surprise: the chip isn't slow at math. It's waiting on memory.
While decoding, it reads from its DDR3 at up to 94 percent of the peak.
So 4-bit weights, fewer bytes per token, made decoding up to 45 percent faster.
